Why didn't the Leaning Tower of Pisa fall? 🇮🇹 Watch 199 years of building in 25 seconds. ⏱️

Work started in 1173 on soft ground with a foundation only about 3 m deep. By the third floor it was already sinking. Then war stopped everything for almost a century, and that pause let the soil settle. Without it, the tower would almost certainly have toppled. When building resumed in 1272, the upper floors were made taller on one side to compensate, so the tower actually curves. The bell chamber went on in 1372.

The twist: by 1990 it leaned 5.5°. Engineers removed about 70 tonnes of soil from under the high side and straightened it to about 4°.

Would you climb it? Yes or no 👇

yt_description:
Foundations laid in August 1173 on soft subsoil; the tower began to sink after the second floor in 1178; war halted work for almost a century, letting the soil settle; building resumed in 1272 with upper floors taller on one side (so it curves); 7th floor 1319, bell chamber 1372. Leaning 5.5° by 1990; 1990–2001 about 70 t of soil was removed from the north side, reducing the lean to ~3.97°.

Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leaning_Tower_of_Pisa · https://everything-everywhere.com/the-leaning-tower-of-pisa/
Figures are historical estimates. Animation is a stylised reconstruction.
